title: Operations Reference Manual: Access, Change, Data, Procurement & Travel
author: Lena Marshall
body:
Overview

This reference manual collects the company-wide operational policies and process templates that teams should follow when requesting access, executing changes, managing data, procuring goods and services, engaging vendors, and booking business travel. The goal is to standardize controls, reduce friction for cross-functional requests, and ensure compliance with our security and financial controls.

Use this page as the canonical index for the day-to-day operational flows and the set of approved templates. If you need a sector-specific deviation (e.g., on-prem deployments or regulated customers), follow the exceptions process documented in the related pages.

Table of contents
1) Principles and responsibilities
2) Access and permissions lifecycle
3) Change management process
4) Data management and classification
5) Procurement and expenses workflow
6) Vendor onboarding & offboarding
7) Travel policy summary and booking flow
8) Templates and forms
9) Exceptions and audit schedule
10) Ownership and escalation

1) Principles and responsibilities

- Least privilege: Access is granted only for the minimum required period and scope to perform the task.
- Segregation of duties: Approvers should be independent of requestors where risk is material.
- Evidence-first: All approvals and receipts must be attached to the request ticket or procurement record.
- Time-boxed access: Temporary elevated privileges must have automatic expiry and audit hooks.
- Cost accountability: Teams owning spend must tag budget codes and follow pre-approval limits.

Roles (quick reference):
- Requestor: initiates requests (access, purchase, travel).
- Manager: technical or functional approver for team-level requests.
- Security Approver: required for privileged access or data classification changes.
- Finance Approver: required for procurement above pre-approved thresholds.
- Vendor Manager: owns vendor contract and SLAs.
- IT Ops / SRE: executes infrastructure changes and runbook updates.

2) Access and permissions lifecycle

Scope: covers access to cloud accounts, internal apps (SaaS), code repositories, databases, and admin consoles.

Required process (step-by-step):
1. Request: Open a ticket in ServiceDesk using the "Access Request" template. Include: resource, desired role, business justification, expiry date, and approval chain.
2. Manager approval: Direct manager must approve via ServiceDesk. If access spans multiple teams, obtain cross-team manager approvals.
3. Security review: For access to sensitive environments (prod, PII, KMS), Security must approve and may require MFA/hardkey enrollment.
4. Provisioning: IT Ops will provision through the identity provider (IdP) and log the IAM change ID.
5. Verification: Requestor verifies access and attaches confirmation to the ticket.
6. Expiry and re-certification: Access granted with an expiry (typically 30/90/365 days by sensitivity). Re-certification reminders are auto-generated 14 days before expiry.

Common thresholds and examples:
- Non-sensitive app access: manager approval, expiry 365 days.
- Prod console access: manager + security approval, expiry 90 days, approved MFA required.
- DB read access to PII: manager + security + data owner approval, expiry 30 days, JIT (just-in-time) provisioning encouraged.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Use the emergency access runbook. Emergency approvals must be logged in the ticket, and a post-incident review must be completed within 72 hours.

3) Change management process

Purpose: provide a predictable, low-risk way to make infrastructure, runtime, or configuration changes. Applies to production, staging, and any environment that supports customer-facing services.

Change types:
- Standard (low-risk, pre-approved routine ops): e.g., SSL cert rotation, scheduled backups.
- Normal (non-emergency but higher risk): requires RFC, impact analysis, and change window.
- Emergency (unplanned critical fixes): follows expedited approval and must be followed by a retrospective.

Normal change workflow (numbered):
1. Create RFC in ChangeTracker with: description, rollback plan, impacted services, SLO impact assessment, contact list, automation scripts, and verification steps.
2. Peer review: at least one technical peer and the SRE owner must review.
3. Scheduling: changes affecting >5% of traffic or customer-visible features require a designated change window and calendar entry.
4. Approvals: SRE lead and Product manager sign off. If change touches sensitive data pathways, Security signs off.
5. Execution: implement according to playbook with an on-call runbook owner present.
6. Verification: smoke tests and telemetry verification, documented in the RFC.
7. Post-change review: within 5 business days for Normal changes; Emergency changes must have a postmortem if an incident occurred.

Key metrics and thresholds:
- All production changes must include an SLO impact estimate.
- Target: >= 95% of Standard changes automated and completed without manual intervention.
- Goal: < 0.5% of Normal changes cause degraded SLO for >15 minutes.

4) Data management and classification

Classification tiers (company standard):
- Public: can be published externally without restriction.
- Internal: company-internal, low risk if exposed.
- Confidential: business-sensitive but not regulated (e.g., unreleased pricing).
- Restricted: regulated or PII/PHI/financial data requiring controls and encryption at rest.

Minimum controls by classification (table-like text):
| Classification | Encryption at rest | Access approval | Retention policy | Audit frequency |
| Public | Optional | Manager | 1 year | Annual random audit |
| Internal | Required (default) | Manager | 3 years | Annual |
| Confidential | Required | Manager + Data Owner | 7 years or as contract | Semi-annual |
| Restricted | Required + KMS | Manager + Security + Data Owner | Contract/Regulation dependent | Quarterly |

Data lifecycle rules:
- Data owners must declare classification at dataset creation.
- Backups inheriting Restricted data must be tracked and rotated per retention rules.
- Data deletions must follow documented procedures and be validated by the owning team.

Data sharing and third parties:
- Any dataset shared with vendors requires a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and Security review.
- Export of Restricted data off-shore requires Legal and Security approval and may be disallowed by region.

5) Procurement and expenses workflow

Principles:
- Centralized visibility: all spend must be recorded in ProcurementHub before purchase.
- Thresholds: defined delegated authority for fast buys vs formal approvals.
- Competitive sourcing: for purchases > $50k, get at least two vendor quotes unless waived by Procurement.

Quick flow (small purchases < $5k):
1. Purchase via corporate card or petty procurement form.
2. Attach receipt to the expense report within 7 days.
3. Manager approves expense.
4. Finance tags cost center.

Medium purchases ($5k–$50k):
1. Create Purchase Request in ProcurementHub with justification, vendor, and budget code.
2. Manager + Finance approval.
3. Procurement issues PO and reconciles invoice.

Large purchases (> $50k):
1. Procurement-led RFP or bidding process.
2. Legal review for contracts and SLAs.
3. Executive approval (VP-level) for strategic vendor relationships.

Expense reimbursement rules:
- Reimbursements require original receipts and an itemized claim.
- Personal charges on corporate card will be flagged and may be reclaimed.

6) Vendor onboarding & offboarding

Onboarding checklist (high level):
1. Vendor intake form in VendorPortal: include scope, data exchanged, key contacts, and financial terms.
2. Security questionnaire (SIG or equivalent) completed by vendor.
3. Legal reviews contract and DPAs as applicable.
4. Finance creates vendor record and payment terms.
5. Procurement finalizes PO and kick-off.
6. Technical integration owned by the consuming team and must include least-privilege credentials.

SLA and monitoring expectations:
- Vendor SLAs for availability and response time must be documented in the contract and tracked in VendorDashboard.
- Quarterly vendor health check with the Vendor Manager for strategic vendors.

Offboarding steps:
- Termination checklist: revoke credentials, remove access from IdP, ensure data return/destruction per contract, finalize outstanding invoices, and document lessons learned.

7) Travel policy summary and booking flow

Purpose: ensure safe, cost-effective business travel with clear approvals and per-diem rules.

Pre-approval steps:
1. Request travel in TravelPortal with dates, purpose, attendees, and estimated cost.
2. Manager approval required. If travel involves a customer or cross-border compliance, Legal must review.
3. For international travel to high-risk regions, Security must review itinerary and provide advisories.

Booking rules:
- Use preferred vendors where discounts exist.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; Premium Economy or Business requires VP approval or for flights >8 hours.
- Hotel bookings should be reasonable and within per-diem caps.

Expenses and receipts:
- Keep detailed receipts for lodging, transport, and meals.
- Itemized meal receipts required for per-diem exceptions.

Safety and emergencies:
- Register travel in TravelPortal to receive security alerts and evacuation assistance.
- In emergencies, follow the Incident Response Security guidance and notify People Ops.

8) Templates and forms

Included templates (attached to this page in Confluence):
- Access Request template (fields: resource, role, justification, expiry, approvers)
- Change RFC template (fields: description, impact, rollback, verification)
- Data Classification declaration (fields: owner, sensitivity, retention)
- Purchase Request form (fields: vendor, itemized costs, quote attachments, budget code)
- Vendor Intake form (fields: contact, DPA required, data flows)
- Travel approval form (fields: purpose, itinerary, estimated cost)

Example snippet: Access Request checklist
1) Resource identifier (URL/ARN)
2) Role requested (exact IAM role)
3) Business justification and duration
4) Manager approval (name + timestamp)
5) Attach verification screenshot after provisioning

9) Exceptions and audit schedule

Exception process:
- Submit an Exception Request with justification, compensating controls, and expiry.
- Exceptions longer than 90 days require Executive sponsor and semi-annual review.

Audit schedule (summary):
- Quarterly: Restricted dataset access review and vendor DPA compliance check.
- Semi-annual: Privileged access recertification for prod consoles.
- Annual: Procurement compliance audit and travel spend analysis.

10) Ownership and escalation

Document owners and contact points:
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (primary), contact: finance-legal@redwood.com
- Security checkpoints and access escalation: security-ops@redwood.com
- Change windows and SRE approvals: platform-sre@redwood.com
- Vendor management: vendor-ops@redwood.com

Escalation matrix (high-level):
1) Team manager -> 2) Department director -> 3) VP of the functional area -> 4) CTO/CFO for unresolved critical items.

Revision history:
- 2024-03-15: Initial publication (Lena Marshall).
- 2024-10-01: Added JIT provisioning guidance and emergency access runbook link.
- 2025-01-10: Updated procurement thresholds and travel comfort rules.

Related resources:
- See the ChangeTracker runbook for templates and automation tricks.
- VendorPortal & ProcurementHub for live requests and status.
- Security Incident Response playbook for emergency break-glass steps.

End of manual. For feedback or to propose edits, file a policy-update ticket and tag Finance & Legal and Security for review.
